about.title: Loomis Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Loomis is a small town of about 6,700 people along Taylor Road, and when someone here dies because of another person's carelessness, the loss ripples through neighbors, schools and churches quickly. Placer County's public collision records for 2025 list 17 injury crashes inside Loomis, 26 people hurt, and one traffic death. Fatal harm also comes from places other than the road: a fall on a poorly kept property, a medical error, a defective product. California treats a wrongful death claim as a civil matter, entirely separate from any criminal charges the district attorney may or may not bring. The claim belongs first to the surviving spouse or domestic partner and children, and then to certain dependents and heirs. It can cover funeral and burial expenses, the financial support the person would have provided, and the love, companionship and guidance that no amount of money truly replaces. LawProactive, a free service rather than a law firm, connects Loomis families with an independent attorney who works on contingency — no fee unless there is a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Loomis Families Reach Out to LawProactive

items.title: Clarity on Who May File
items.desc: California limits standing in wrongful death cases, giving priority to the surviving spouse or domestic partner and children before certain dependents and heirs. An attorney can sort out who belongs in the claim before anyone files.

items.title: Deadlines Tracked From Day One
items.desc: The general filing window is two years from the date of death, but it shrinks considerably when a city, county or state agency is involved. Early attention keeps a grieving family from losing rights they did not know they had.

items.title: Every Category of Loss Counted
items.desc: Recoverable losses include funeral and burial costs, the income and support the person would have provided, and the love, companionship and guidance the family has lost. The attorney's job is to make sure none of that is left out.

items.question: My husband was killed in a crash on Horseshoe Bar Road. Does the criminal case decide our claim?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a civil action and moves forward on its own track, whether or not the Placer County District Attorney files charges or the other driver is convicted. The evidence can overlap, but the standard of proof and the goal are different. Your attorney can pursue the civil side while the criminal process runs its course.

items.question: Who is allowed to bring a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: The surviving spouse or registered domestic partner and the children have the first right to file. If there is no one in that group, certain financially dependent relatives and heirs may step in. Because the rules are specific, it is wise to have an attorney confirm who qualifies before a case is opened.

items.question: How long do we have to act after a death in Loomis?
items.answer: In most situations the deadline is two years from the date of death, not from the date of the crash or injury. If a government entity — say a county road agency or a public hospital — may be responsible, a claim must usually be presented in far less time, often within six months. Reaching out early protects those options while you focus on your family.
